advisory.text:
Air quality in the Delhi/Karachi region (NW India + Pakistan) is currently Very Unhealthy for a significant portion of the population, with estimates indicating that approximately 79% of the region has satellite coverage. This affects around 117.7 million people, with the northern eastern part experiencing the highest pollution levels at ~197 µg/m³, followed by the northern western part (~136 µg/m³) and the southern eastern part (~122 µg/m³). 

Vulnerable groups such as children, the elderly, and individuals with pre-existing respiratory conditions are at increased risk from air pollution. To mitigate this, we recommend:

1. Stay indoors if possible, especially for those sensitive to air pollution.
2. Use high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filters in your homes to purify the air.

Please remember that these estimates, not measurements, are based on available satellite data and may not reflect real-time conditions in all areas. It's crucial to stay updated from reliable local health authorities for the most accurate information.
